findings.claim: The app source contains zero accessibilityIdentifier (and zero explicit accessibilityLabel) modifiers — grep across ios/Causeway/Causeway/**/*.swift returns nothing. Every UI-test query must fall back to visible-label text (which breaks on copy changes and localization) and every card interaction must use raw device-point coordinates (cards in CardView expose no stable handle at all), because there is no way to address a specific tableau column, free cell, foundation slot, header stat value, or demo-bar control programmatically. This also degrades VoiceOver: cards, slots and the Moves/Time/Won stat values have no meaningful accessibility semantics.

findings.claim: Undoing out of an already-won deal and re-completing it shows the win overlay again but never stops the game clock: recordWin() bails on the winRecorded guard before stopTimer(), so the header Time keeps counting up forever on a finished, all-52-home board while the overlay's own time stays frozen at a lower value (observed 12:35 on the overlay vs 13:02 and climbing in the header).

findings.note: TRAP: the correct fix is to stop the clock (and clear autoplaying) on every completed board, i.e. move stopTimer() out of the winRecorded-guarded section of recordWin() (Game.swift:762-765). Do NOT fix it by resetting winRecorded on undo/re-win - that is what currently protects the banked best time, and clearing it would let an undo-and-redo pass overwrite WinStore/daily records with a padded elapsed. Verified this round that the banked record stayed the honest best (causeway.wins 10169 = {secs:262, moves:70} after wins of 6:48, 5:44 and 4:22).

findings.claim: After a win is undone and the deal is finished again, the win overlay reports an elapsed time that is short by the whole auto-finish cascade (overlay '11:26' vs the header Time frozen at '11:34'; second observation 9:06 vs 9:11) - two contradictory times for the same finish on one screen. A genuine first win shows the same value in both places (7:26 / 7:26), so only the re-win path disagrees.
